text: This will be a goodbye for us, friend. The voidship you see out there will carry us through time and space, to those who need imperfections and assistance. We will become chronographers, those who chart and upkeep time. As a last wish, I ask one final favor of you.
You have sealed your fate!
Growl!
result_script: ;this prevents werewolves from talking to you in combat

text: Yes, I'm a Dwemer. Did the beard give it away?

The Dwemer are the fabled lost Dwarven race whose ruins and splendid artifacts are scattered across Tamriel. Elves use the term "Dwemer," connoting variously "deep-delving," "profound," and "close-counseled"; Imperial usage is "Dwarven," derived in fable from the affectionate regard of the Giant races for their "little" Dwemer friends. There are several Dwemer sites on Vvardenfell, and many have found Dwemer artifacts.
The Angry Bones are no longer angry, I see. I shall have... words, with my followers about augmentations, but for now, I suppose we should celebrate.
The dead rest once more.
The dead.

There are four factions in my district who oversee most of the day-to-day operations. The Watch, the Wonder, the Build, and the Tear Down. I wish for you interview the heads of each, with my explicit permission, and see if they know anything about these undead attacks. Remember, keep an open mind, as those fabricants are often... eccentric. And take care if you venture out during the night.

Someone has tampered with things they should not. While my temple and the surrounding buildings have often disagreed on many points, something or someone has violated laws we all hold sacred, and the consequences are felt and seen throughout. Angry Bones walk the streets at night, spilling out of the catacombs, furious at something.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Temple District
text: Finally, we have quite a few retired priests living on the southeast outer ring. Goveri-999, the mer who wrote that book about rewounds, lives there.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Temple District
text:
The inner ring houses the headquarters of the four factions in the city. Going clockwise from the top left corner, you have the Watch, the Wonder, the Build, and the Tear Down. They don't provide services to non-members normally, but a few of them have set up shops here and there.
In the back, the far left corner that is, we have the dual-tavern, the Kneeling Mechanism, and the Creeping Grapevine. Both offer drinks to the thirsty. The center building is of course, the Temple, where the Archcanon is.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Temple District
text:
Ah, The Temple District! Quite clean, isn't it? Of course, that just suggests a deeper evil, but I'm not an adventurer, so what do I know?
At any rate, you can think of this district like a miniature version of the rest of the city; it has shops, homes, and shrines. Let's go over them.

The Temple District is opposite the Hub District. It houses the main Temple, which is the seat of power in the Clockwork City, as well as access to the catacombs, where our dead are kept. If the Hub is the heart of our city, then the Temple is our soul.

The Tribunal Temple is the native religion. They worship three God-Kings, Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec, who are known together as the Tribunal. We usually just call it 'The Temple.' They're narrow-minded and superstitious, but I find a lot to admire -- particularly their concern for the poor. They accept outlanders as members, but few outlanders join except for the services. Talk to Feldrelo Sadri at the Balmora Temple if you're thinking about joining.
(He freezes, then pantomimes an exaggerated sigh.)

It will be difficult to overcome the Dunmer's lingering resentment of Imperial occupation. Ironically, it is now, in the face of the menace of Dagoth Ur and Red Mountain, that we have a great opportunity to unite natives and colonists against a common threat. When the Dunmer fight side by side with outlanders like you against the hosts of Dagoth Ur, our common peril and purpose must unite us.

You see, Nerevar, the Regent is the highest of Intelligences. All things in the city answer to him, and all mechanisms are, indirectly, controlled by him. He is the Taskmaster, the Overseer, the Central Processor, and without him, the city may function, but it will eventually break. If he is broken, then the rest of this world will follow in his nonexistent footsteps.

He calls himself Gestalt now? Very troubling. Gestalt implies something greater, something larger. A change in name after so much change in the city itself is most upsetting. If he reached this conclusion of his own doing, then we have little to worry about, but if this change is brought by the change that changed the city, then he may be damaged.

And thus, this class struggle makes no natural sense. The have and the have-nots now fight and jeer constantly, rather than work side-by-side, to either keep or achieve wealth. At first, I thought myself incorrect, or otherwise wrong, about our social structure. Then, it became more apparent. As fabricants are not naturally conflictuous, which is a word I have made up, the only way for them to fight as such would require an outside force. In conclusion, my colleagues and I believe someone encouarges this.

I believe in the natural, or the otherwise living and growing. It is why I lead the Abstemious, and why I study our people and culture. We are perhaps in that though there are fabricants who are poor, and fabricants who are rich, but all started on the same level. We are a merit-based society, in which those who are inventive rise, and those who are lazy, or otherwise incompetent, fall. To this extent, jealousy is nonexistent, and in the few cases that is, or otherwise present, it is not over wealth.

I see. So you have reached a dead end, or are unable to find any more evidence? Perhaps there is no more to be found. If such a thing is true, or otherwise correct, we should pursue another possible line that may lead us to the culprit. Let us speak of pamphlets.

Please, I beg you, don't kill me! Yes, I distributed the drugs, but I don't know where I got them from! They would show up in my house, with instructions! I assumed that I was just doing the work of our Lord! I don't even get the crates any more! Please, spare me!
Wha- Not going to kill me? Oh. Well. Excuse me then, I have to go change my pants.

My warehouse is located above my manor, simply go west through the doors until you reach the dining hall, then north into the elevator. From there, head east across the bridge atop the manor, and enter the tower on the east end.

Moon sugar, you say? Well I do know OF the substance, I had invented an engine in my youth that was powered by skooma, but I do not deal in such substances. It is beneath me. But, ah, of course, I should have expected this. You see, my friend, I have the privilege of owning the only warehouse in the entire district. I found it only proper to loan it out to various others to use for their own storage. You are of course, welcome to poke around and find your sugar crates, and perhaps their owner.

Well, we know each other, I guess it wouldn't hurt. I see some folks selling it occasionally, it ain't against the law after all, it's fine if they are. They talk about picking up crates of the stuff at a warehouse on the other side of town, owned by someone named Relamus I think? Don't know the guy, but any drug dealer is bad news.
Addicts? Moon sugar? Look, I understand if you're trying to do something, but I'm not about to tell some wanderer about people I know, it looks bad on my tavern.

Whasat? Ah go away you s'wit fetchering n'wah or... what's the point. You got any moon sugar? Oh but are ya y'know... willing to buy some for me? There was that place, down there, the brothel. Or is it a bar? Setley's Wonders or whatever it is. There's a girl there who can take off BOTH her legs, I tell ya.
But that's where I first got my hit of the stuff. Now go away, ants are starting to attack m'feet.

An addict would have to find his star pepper from a supplier, who would in turn have a source. Find one, and follow the trail, or otherwise track it. Remember, as an addict, they would no doubt have lost everything, merely to fund their addiction. We fabricants are not used to narcotics, so those that are under their influence, or otherwise addicted, fall hard.

Well yes, of course, I'm made of metal aren't I? And only statues are made of metal! Therefore, I am a statue, now if you'll excuse me, I must continue being a statue. But I can't talk! Statues can't talk.
Very well. If you wish to participate, however, my door is always open.
Excellent, let's begin!

I would cast spells on you, and see the effects on your body, and then I'd pay you for it. Simple enough, but there is a catch. These spells are harmful, or outright damaging. There is a risk of death, but the pay is good. I'll leave it up to you though, do you want to be my experimental minion?
Though you have quartz, you do not have enough.

I take it. I break it. Now, I make it.
Here is your quartz.

PlaySound "conjuration hit"
Player-> RemoveItem "sotha_quartz" 3
Player-> Additem "sotha_quartz_boots" 1
Goodbye

text: Mine the quartz. Use the pickaxe I gave you.

I make it. I need it. I lack the parts. I have a pickaxe. In all the districts, blue quartz lies. Find it in districts. Bring it to me. I will pay you.
No. Better. I will trade you armor pieces for it.

Quartz is a rare, powerful and heavy material, immune to the effects of time, and thus perfect for armor. However, it takes time to smith, is very heavy, and only the purest quartz can be used. A full set in Sotha Sil would be very rare

You say you've found someone to upload my mind? And a good one. Well, excellent!
Thank, I mean, thank you so much! I shall go there immediately! Here, friend, take this. It's not much, and I'm not even sure if it's mine exactly, but you deserve it!
A transicant creation? I've done a few in my lifetime, they're easy enough. Of course, there is the matter of the fee.
I'm not letting you do any sort of 'uploading'. I want a professional

I suppose I have reason to trust you. The process is... painless, right? Good.
But you know, I don't think you know how to turn someone into a fabricant. I didn't think so. But do you know some who does?
What? No. That's unnatural, that's disgusting! Why would I do such a thing? What if I die? What if it fails and I'm left a shadow of my former self? I'd rather just wait out a way to go home.
I thought about painting my arms grey, but... you know.
result_script: Choice "Tell him about uploading his mind into a fabricant body" 1

text: I. DO. NOT. RESIST. ORDERS. OR. CHANGE. MY. ONLY. GOAL. IS. TO. TEACH. THROUGH. PUNISHMENT. ACTIONS. HAVE. CONSEQUENCES. IF. YOU. WISH. TO. SHUT. DOWN. ALL. WATCHMEN. I. WOULD. NOT. STOP. YOU. BUT. HEAR. MY. WORDS.

All fabricants and transicants have, deep inside of us, a small thing called a pneuma. It not only holds our soul, but acts as a life-force. If our bodies are destroyed, but the pneuma survives, our souls may be placed inside a new body.
Of course, the energy in the pneuma will naturally fade, and we all will eventually die of old age. But such is life.
They believe in studying everything, and are very... impractical. Nonetheless, they are charitable, and always friendly.

It is said that Sotha Sil was curious about everything, that everything was full of wonder, and knowledge. And oh, how true it is! We of the Wonder seek to know the intricacies of everything, be it machine or plant, and thus, we study to build up our knowledge.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Temple District
text:
Weirdos if anything. They're the smallest of the factions in the Temple District, and believe in studying and recording everything. And I do mean everything. They have an entire section dedicated to skulls, I hear, which just demonstrates how weird they are. 
Still, wonder and record is almost all they do, so it's not like one can complain.

Weirdos if anything. They're the smallest of the factions in the Temple District, and believe in studying and recording everything. And I do mean everything. They have an entire section dedicated to skulls, I hear, which just demonstrates how weird they are. 
Still, wonder and record is almost all they do, so it's not like one can complain.
We're watching you. Scum.
Go. Now.
Go on about your business.
If you're here for trouble, you'll get more than you bargained for.
Growl!

Aye, inside of me! Not like that though. Like the other that! Hah! Got me a distillererery, or whatever, in my belly. Booze whenever I want, even when I don't. 
(He taps his belly, which makes a hollow metallic sound.)
It can't do wine for some reason. Shame, really, 'cause I'd kill for some wine.
I'm not a drinker myself.
Gears!
Gears?
The mad made sane.
The mad.
While I'm grateful for a solved problem, it leaves me with little to do.
I'd stay out of them all the same, if I were you.
Hm. This is pass certainly LOOKS official. What would the Archcanon need with a district of madmen? Ah well, it's not my place to wonder, merely to watch. I'll let the guards know to let you in.

I suppose I have reason to trust you. Very well, I will let the Watchmen know. As your friend, however, I advise you to stay out of the district unless you absolutely must enter. That place is an absolute deathtrap at the moment.

You say the Archcanon has given you permission to enter?
I highly doubt that. Show me anything, a piece of paper, a token: prove to me he has allowed this. No pass? Well, then no entry.
As I've said, access is restricted. I would say more, but I'm under orders.

Perhaps it should not surprise you that once cured, the denizens of the Slums would not look upon you with adoration for murdering their friends and family, even if it was self-defense. Normally, I would be hesitant to offer a solution, but...
The Slums once served as a great social experiment for Sotha Sil, to study the forces that govern life and love. At the four corners of this district are shrines that serve as a reset mechanism. If you could activate them, it would purge the systems of your crime.
I have heard of your success in the slums. If I were more inclined towards research, I would mourn the loss of the Pocket Cabal, but such a terrible entity deserved nothing but complete destruction.
I have given you a pass. Use it how you wish.

Of all the... It seems even the Hub is not immune to the troubles of the city. Here. This note should suffice and grant you access to the slums. Hopefully, the madness has not spread to the transfer guardians, or we will all be in severe trouble.

It was once a place of peace, though not of prosperity. One could once walk down its streets unharmed; now, this is no longer the case. Something has turned the citizens of the slums into madmen, little more than zombies shambling through ruined streets, and I have ordered it to be sealed. If you manage to enter the slums and rid it of the source of this lunacy, then no doubt it will return to normal.

Everything's cleared up there, apparently. People are starting to move back and it's going back to normal, thanks to your efforts. Thank you for aiding all of us, not just the fabricants living there.

Not a very nice name for a district, is it? It housed most of the fabricants in the city, at least, until everything there went a bit mad. No-one's entirely sure what happened, only that some people started malfunctioning and attacking everything around them. And then there's that great tower in the center of the district; no-one really knows what its function is, as no-one has entered it in living memory. It's kept permanently locked.
We discussed this.
I am not one for many words. You are rumored to be good at ending things. We will work well together. And for the start of our work, we must analyze these surges!
Well of course! Look at all this water! Goes on for hundreds of miles! And the fog, don't even get me started on the fog! What do you mean we're just in a house? Bah, you've gone sea-crazy, friend!

Indeed. I can talk to animals, you see. And they talk back. It's an excellent tool for farming, and it helps me know what the stock want. People think I'm just a bit unhinged, but the stock say I'm not, so obviously I can't be.

Yessir, yes ma'am! Today, one day only, I have these INCREDIBLE wares, on sale, for you! Like this legendary goblet of legend! Just a cup you say? Well take a look at THESE! Ancient Akavir weapons! You think they're just dinner forks? Well I can see you will not be fooled, so take a look at THESE dwemer artifacts! Okay they're dwemer spoons, but they're artifacts nonetheless!
I. AM. THE. VOICE. OF. JUSTICE. IN. THE. CITY. THE. WATCHMEN. RESPOND. TO. ME. I. AM. THEIR. HEART. AND. THEIR. SOUL.

Funny name, isn't it, but 'emerald computation arraymesh mail' is a bit of a mouthful. There's a lot of failed projects in Sotha Sil, and if you're a smart smith, you can take the thrown out bits and recycle them into a set of armor. It's very durable while still being relatively lightweight, and being made of old magical machinery makes it a good choice if you were able to enchant it.
Seers essentially. They worship the side of Sotha Sil that saw the future, and seek to emulate him, by seeing all. Foolish, but harmless.
We of the Watch watch. Is it not said that Sotha Sil himself could see through time, both in the before and the after? We seek to emulate this, but to do so, we must first see in the now.

text:
They call themselves observers. Really they're perverts. They watch everything and everything, but yet never tell anyone what they're doing. 
Makes you wonder really.

They call themselves observers. Really they're perverts. They watch everything and everything, but yet never tell anyone what they're doing. 
Makes you wonder really.
Builders and workers for the temple. They are very religious, yet also very intelligent and creative. One of the few factions I approve of.
